creatures.name: Puffgrub
creatures.flavor: Rolls through the grass eating grass, offering nothing, fearing everything.

behaviour.idle: Ambles peacefully between patches of ground, paying no attention to any other creature nearby, including the player.
behaviour.when_locked: Bolts instantly in a straight, dead-simple sprint the moment it's locked -- no zig-zag, no hesitation, and no fighting back, ever.

creatures.flavor: Half mud, half meat, all squeal.

creatures.name: Scrawny Thumper
creatures.flavor: All knuckles and no neck, it complains right up until it doesn't.

behaviour.idle: Grazes and lumbers in a loose, unhurried huddle, sticking close to two or three others of its own kind rather than wandering alone.
behaviour.when_locked: Breaks into a heavy, slower panic-run than the others, zig-zagging in short lurches rather than sharp cuts -- easy to read, but its bulk means it takes longer to actually get away.

creatures.flavor: Twitchy legs, empty head, gone before you blink twice.

behaviour.idle: Never really stands still -- hops and shuffles on the spot even at rest, always half-ready to bolt.
behaviour.when_locked: Explodes into a full sprint with sudden, sharp zig-zags and direction reversals the instant it's locked -- the hardest of the prey to run down in a straight chase.

creatures.flavor: One good eye and a better trigger; useless the second you're inside its arms.

behaviour.idle: Keeps its distance from clumps of other creatures, drifting at the edges of open ground where it has room to see and run.
behaviour.when_locked: Flees in wide, looping zig-zags that favour open ground over cover, always trying to keep space between itself and the chaser.

creatures.name: Scrawny Skulker
creatures.flavor: Slinks in, bites once, forgets to leave a body.

behaviour.idle: Shifts and skulks near terrain features -- rocks, reeds, treelines -- in a loose, watchful gaggle rather than a tight herd.
behaviour.when_locked: Panics into sharp, unpredictable zig-zags and doubles back behind whatever cover is nearest; when one is locked, the rest of its gaggle scatters in different directions instead of bunching up.

creatures.name: Scrawny Greymaw
creatures.flavor: Doesn't have a weak side, and hates that you keep looking for one.

behaviour.idle: Moves with an unhurried confidence the other prey don't have -- it doesn't startle at nearby movement the way softer prey does.
behaviour.when_locked: Flees in a measured, testing retreat rather than blind panic -- still a zig-zag, but deliberate, probing for the gap that lets it break the lock.

creatures.name: The Knucklebreaker
creatures.flavor: Picks a fight with the ground first, just to prove it can lose and get up anyway.

behaviour.territory: Plants itself over a fixed patch of ground inside its pocket and rarely leaves it; pursues intruders only within that patch and settles back onto the same spot once they're gone.
behaviour.wind_up: Digs in, braces its whole body, and keeps closing the distance steadily through the wind-up -- slow to commit but very hard to outrun once it does.

creatures.name: The Redline Ripper
creatures.flavor: Hits top speed somewhere between your first step back and your last.

behaviour.territory: Patrols a wider loop around its pocket rather than holding one spot, the most mobile of the elites while on guard.
behaviour.wind_up: Crouches low into a visible coil and then closes the gap almost immediately -- the shortest, hardest-to-react-to wind-up of any elite.

creatures.name: The Deadeye Warden
creatures.flavor: Already locked onto you before you noticed the grass move.

behaviour.territory: Perches at the edge of its pocket with clear sightlines across the open ground it guards, rather than lurking in the thick of it.
behaviour.wind_up: Rears back and holds its reach out toward the locked target, closing only as much distance as it needs before its long-reach pounce connects.

creatures.name: The Throatgrin
creatures.flavor: You won't hear it coming. You'll just stop being able to breathe.

behaviour.territory: Shifts position among the pocket's cover instead of holding one spot, never staying in the open for long.
behaviour.wind_up: Weaves in on an unpredictable line while closing, making the moment it commits to the pounce harder to time against than a straight approach.

creatures.name: The Ashmaw
creatures.flavor: Doesn't have a specialty. Doesn't need one.

behaviour.territory: Holds the deepest, most central ground in its pocket -- the anchor point the rest of the pocket is built around.
behaviour.wind_up: Closes steadily and evenly through the wind-up with no obvious tell to exploit, matching its all-round strength.

creatures.name: The Mudking
creatures.flavor: Rules a puddle like an ocean, and will drown you just to prove the point.

behaviour.arena: Holds the deep marsh hollow it dens in, staying close to open water it can use against you; it never abandons this ground, however the fight goes.
behaviour.opening: The fight usually starts while the hollow's other occupants are already closing in from around the pond.
behaviour.wind_up: Rears up out of the water or mud into a full brace before lunging -- unmistakable even through the murk, and it never flees the exchange.

creatures.name: The Cragfather
creatures.flavor: Older than the rocks it squats on, meaner than every single one of them.

behaviour.arena: Holds its rocky outcrop and uses the height of it, sticking near ledges rather than open ground; it does not give up this crag no matter how the fight turns.
behaviour.opening: Usually engaged while other outcrop-dwellers are already closing in from the rocks around it.
behaviour.wind_up: Digs its claws into the stone and hunches low before an explosive lunge along or down the outcrop, and stands its ground through the whole exchange.

creatures.name: The Frostback
creatures.flavor: Grew a second hide out of spite for the cold, then started collecting more.
creatures.habitat: the foothills, below the lethal cold line

behaviour.arena: Prowls the foothills below the snowline, patrolling the same ground the local grazers use; it never breaks off this territory.
behaviour.opening: Typically starts while nearby foothill occupants are already converging on you.
behaviour.wind_up: Plants its shaggy bulk, lowers its head, and holds a short, heavy pause before a full charge -- and it does not flee once committed.

creatures.name: The Cinderjaw
creatures.flavor: Breathes the vent like air and looks at you like lunch.

behaviour.arena: Guards the volcanic vents along the shore, staying close to the heat and glow it lives on; it never abandons the vents, win or lose.
behaviour.opening: Usually engaged while other vent-dwellers are already closing in around you.
behaviour.wind_up: The scorched seam across its face flares brighter as it braces, then it lunges -- and it never breaks off the fight.

creatures.name: Bonelord of the Trampled Fields
creatures.flavor: All knuckles and no neck, it complains right up until it doesn't.

behaviour.emergence: The den lights, the ground trembles, and an audio cue rises well before it appears; once both gates close, there is a short grace period before the lair erupts and it steps out.
behaviour.hunt: Slow but utterly relentless -- it doesn't need to be fast because it can never be outrun; it closes steadily across the whole biome, wherever you are, with heavy, clearly telegraphed pounces.
behaviour.tell: The stirring lair is the only warning: lights, tremor, rising sound, well before it emerges.

creatures.name: Quickfang of the Trampled Fields
creatures.flavor: Twitchy legs, empty head, gone before you blink twice.

behaviour.emergence: The den lights, the ground trembles, and an audio cue rises before the gates close; a short grace period follows, then the lair erupts and it emerges.
behaviour.hunt: Blisteringly fast out of the gate -- it closes distance almost the moment it emerges, hunting you across the whole biome with no wasted movement.
behaviour.tell: The stirring lair -- lights, tremor, rising sound -- is your only notice before it comes.

creatures.name: Deadeye of the Trampled Fields
creatures.flavor: One good eye and a better trigger; useless the second you're inside its arms.

behaviour.emergence: The den lights, the ground trembles, and an audio cue rises before both gates close; then a short grace period, then the lair erupts and it emerges.
behaviour.hunt: Hangs at the edge of its own reach as it hunts you across the biome, stalking from outside your comfortable range and punishing any moment you let it line up.
behaviour.tell: The stirring lair -- lights, tremor, rising sound -- is the only warning before it appears.

creatures.name: Nightthroat of the Trampled Fields
creatures.flavor: Slinks in, bites once, forgets to leave a body.

behaviour.emergence: The den lights, the ground trembles, and an audio cue rises before the gates close; a short grace period follows, then the lair erupts.
behaviour.hunt: Takes an unpredictable path across the whole biome as it hunts, weaving in and out of your route so its approach is hard to call in advance.
behaviour.tell: The stirring lair -- lights, tremor, rising sound -- is your only notice before it emerges.

creatures.name: Greytyrant of the Trampled Fields
creatures.flavor: Doesn't have a weak side, and hates that you keep looking for one.

behaviour.emergence: The den lights, the ground trembles, and an audio cue rises before both gates close; then a short grace period, then the lair erupts and it steps out.
behaviour.hunt: Dangerous on every axis as it hunts you across the whole biome -- no obvious weak angle to it, closing steadily and evenly wherever you run.
behaviour.tell: The stirring lair -- lights, tremor, rising sound -- is the only warning you get before it appears.
